answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule: each identity's action distribution is hashed into a rotating kernel that seeds the next epoch's challenge set, so an attacker must sustain matching behaviour across epochs rather than pass once. A lantern score tracks divergence between an identity's predicted and actual response patterns, and identities whose divergence exceeds a threshold get throttled or excluded from rewards. Buying fresh identities costs the full training period per sybil because each must independently build a consistent history to unlock the opal tier of resource access.
